1. Case 1: Hemiconvulsion-hemiplegia
A 5-month-old girl with normal prior development developed fever, then a 10–15-hour refractory seizure and persistent left hemiparesis that improved with antiepileptics. MRI right hemicerebral diffusion restriction with normal left cortex and normal MRA indicates unilateral postictal edema, not large-vessel stroke; normal MRA argues against acute ischemic stroke.
